A1.justification: Both are readable 11-page versions of the same STCast paper, with corresponding text, equations, figures and tables. However, both reference an Appendix containing additional details and experiments that neither supplied PDF includes. The judgments below cover the supplied material.

before.justification: v2 reports original global and regional forecasting experiments, typhoon predictions, ensemble results and ablations in Section 4, Tables 1–5 and Figures 5–9.

after.justification: v3 retains these original forecasting experiments and ablation results, including numerical evaluations of STCast.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same STCast architecture, Spatial-Aligned Attention, Gaussian month-conditioned Temporal Mixture-of-Experts, and Perlin-noise ensemble procedure.

E1.justification: Both use ERA5 for global and Eastern Asia regional forecasting, evaluate the 2024 Ewiniar and Yinxing typhoons, and retain the same long-range and ensemble forecasting scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the reported comparisons. Tables 1 and 3 retain Pangu, Graphcast, Fuxi and OneForecast; regional comparisons retain Direct Train and OneForecast, and Figures 5 and 9 retain their respective comparator sets.

E3.justification: The reported training period, variable counts, 100-epoch budget, batch size 16, forecast horizons and evaluation metrics are unchanged. Ensemble evaluation still uses the same 10 initial conditions described in Section 4.2.

E4.justification: Both retain the component ablations in Table 2, expert-count and embedding comparisons in Table 4, distance-metric comparisons in Table 5, and spatial-error and 100-day forecast visualizations in Figures 6–8.

E5.justification: Ensemble sampling and averaging descriptions are unchanged. Neither version adds training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or other statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The numerical tables, plotted curves and qualitative forecast maps are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports STCast's 10-day RMSE/ACC as 0.5763/0.4715 in both, and Figure 9 reports the same 96.5 km average Yinxing track error.

T1.justification: The task definitions and mathematical formulations in Section 3, including distance, attention and Gaussian-routing equations (1)–(7), are unchanged. No theorem, proof or derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces 'state-of-the-art methods' with 'other methods' while retaining the same superiority claim across four tasks. The introduction's state-of-the-art contribution claim and the conclusion remain unchanged, leaving the substantive contribution and claim scope intact.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations involving adaptive boundaries and monthly expert specialization, along with the accuracy-versus-parameter tradeoff supporting 12 experts. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit STCast code-repository link at the end of the abstract; v2 has no such link. Training and hardware disclosures remain unchanged. The PDFs establish the added access information but do not establish the repository's contents or usability.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 52 bibliography entries are unchanged. Positioning relative to OneForecast and earlier mixture-of-experts forecasting methods is retained.

P1.justification: v3 makes a small abstract edit, updates the author/contact line to identify corresponding authors, and adds Section 6, Acknowledgements. The scientific narrative and existing section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 removes printed page numbers, adjusts the first-page text layout, and reflows the bibliography around the new acknowledgements. Figures 1–9 and Tables 1–5 retain their displays, captions and placement.

improvement.justification: The explicit code-access pointer and new funding acknowledgements modestly improve documentation and transparency. Scientific methods, evidence and analyses remain unchanged. The referenced appendix is still absent, and code usability cannot be established from the supplied PDFs, so the supported improvement is limited.
